successors.name: Hittite Empire
successors.text: the Arzawa lands, 'fully subjugated by the Hittites around 1300 BC, after an unsuccessful rebellion'; Mira, Hapalla and the Seha River Land continued as Hittite vassal kingdoms

ledger.x: 1700 BC: Arzawa appears in Western Anatolia with its capital at Apasa.

c. 1400 BC: Arzawa is subjugated by Tudhaliya I/II. 'they were subjugated by Tudhaliya I/II around 1400 BC, concurrently with the Assuwa Revolt'; the Assuwa page dates the 22-state western confederation to 'around 1400 BC'. The page says 'subjugated', not annexed or ruled by a governor, so it is drawn as vassalage…

c. 1370 BC: Arzawa acts independently again (bridging judgment; the page gives no end to the subjugation). The next dated statement is that 'Around 1370 BC, during the reign of Tudhaliya III, Arzawa conquered a large portion of Western Anatolia', which presupposes freedom from Hatti.

c. 1370 BC: Arzawa conquers a large part of Western Anatolia. 'Around 1370 BC, during the reign of Tudhaliya III, Arzawa conquered a large portion of Western Anatolia.' ledger.x: c. 1320 BC: Mursili II and Uhha-Ziti fight for the Arzawa lands. Mursili II acceded in 1321 BC ('1321-1295 BC' short chronology) and 'turned to the West to resist the aggression of Uhhaziti, king of Arzawa'; the Arzawa page dates Uhha-Ziti to 1320-1300 BC and says 'When Mursili II ascended to the Hittite throne, much…

c. 1300 BC: the Hittites end the war. 'The Arzawa lands were fully subjugated by the Hittites around 1300 BC, after an unsuccessful rebellion.' Mursili II installed Mashuiluwa at Mira (Mira page) and treaties survive with Kupanta-Kurunta of Mira, Targasnalli of Hapalla and Manapa-Tarhunta of the Seha River Land.

c. 1300 BC: Arzawa passes to Hatti, its pieces as vassal kingdoms. 'fully subjugated by the Hittites around 1300 BC'; Mira ('ca. 1330-1190 BC', 'one of the semi-autonomous vassal state kingdoms that emerged in western Anatolia'), Hapalla and the Seha River Land continue under Hittite overlords. wars.name: Hattusili I's raid on Arzawa
wars.outcome: A raid with no recorded territorial result.

wars.name: Tudhaliya I/II's western campaign and the Assuwa Revolt
wars.outcome: Arzawa 'subjugated by Tudhaliya I/II around 1400 BC'; the Assuwa confederation of 22 states 'was defeated under Tudhaliya I/II'.

wars.name: Suppiluliuma I's campaigns against Arzawa
wars.outcome: No recorded territorial result; Suppiluliuma 'continued to campaign against Arzawa' and installed pro-Hittite rulers in former Arzawan vassal states such as Mira (undated).

wars.name: Mursili II's Arzawa campaign
wars.outcome: Hittite victory: Uhha-Ziti flees and dies in exile; the Arzawa lands are 'fully subjugated by the Hittites around 1300 BC' and become the vassal kingdoms of Mira, Hapalla and the Seha River Land.

certainty.note: No border is described on any page opened; every Arzawa frontier is an approximate reading of the named lands.
